A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same OmniCamera work. Their main sections, equations, tables, and figures can be matched reliably. V1 includes supplementary Sections I–III; v2 ends with references without those sections. This is an observable omission, not an extraction gap.

before.justification: V1 reports original video-generation evaluations in Tables 3–7, supplementary component ablations in Table 9, and qualitative experimental comparisons.

after.justification: V2 retains the original quantitative evaluations in Tables 3–7 and qualitative generation, modality-conflict, and ablation results.

M1.justification: The model, Condition RoPE, dual-level curriculum, and dual-condition CFG remain unchanged in Sections 3.3–3.5. Removing supplementary preprocessing and sparse-injection details reduces documentation but does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use OmniCAM's synthetic and real-world data and retain the nine combinations of content and camera-control modalities. The omitted camera-motion library table describes existing coverage; its removal does not establish that any motion classes or tasks were dropped.

E2.justification: The benchmark comparator sets in Tables 3–5 remain unchanged. However, supplementary Figures 13–14 disappear, removing evaluated comparisons against Channel Concat, KV-Concat, Dense Injection, and Deep MLP.

E3.justification: Retained experiments specify the same 5B model, resolution, 60K training steps, batch size, 36 inputs per camera modality, and 800 generated videos per task. No replacement protocol is stated. Omitted alignment, metric, and human-evaluation descriptions represent lost disclosure rather than demonstrated procedural changes.

E4.justification: V2 removes supplementary Section III: RoPE and dual-condition CFG ablations across six task/control combinations, plus content-injection and camera-injection comparisons. Table 9 and Figures 12–14 are absent. The main curriculum, data-composition, and modality-conflict analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. Removing supplementary point estimates does not change uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 3–7 retain identical scores, but v2 removes Table 9's component-ablation results across six task/control combinations. For example, trajectory-controlled T2V FVD values of 1108.62 without RoPE and 902.45 without dual-condition CFG disappear. Figures 12–14 also remove qualitative findings about positional interference and injection-strategy failures.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4) and the Condition RoPE mathematics retain their meaning; renaming r_complex to r_comp is not substantive. The omitted supplementary Equation (5) states standard trajectory-error formulas, while its alignment discussion supplies implementation details rather than new theory or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about unified camera/content control, OmniCAM, curriculum co-training, and improved controllability with competitive visual quality. Removing supporting supplementary evidence does not revise those claims.

C2.justification: V2 removes supplementary explanations linking dense-injection instability to VAE compression, KV-Concat weaknesses to insufficient semantic information, and dual-condition CFG mainly to control accuracy. Main interpretations and the limitation concerning multiple reference images and localized motion guidance remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 loses filtering thresholds of 5 and 3.0, trajectory-alignment and degenerate-motion handling, canonical-template details, the complete motion library, raw-video and candidate-matching counts, metric calculations, human MotionAcc assessment details, and the one-in-five-block camera-injection schedule. Section 4.1 also changes '32 H100 GPUs' to '32 GPUs', reducing hardware specificity without establishing different hardware.

R1.justification: Five supplement-only references disappear: Sturm et al., Umeyama, Unterthiner et al., SV4D, and VideoGPT. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged; other citation renumbering and venue wording changes do not introduce different works.

P1.justification: The main prose and section sequence remain essentially verbatim. V2 corrects the placeholder running title, shortens complexity notation, removes the corresponding-author footnote, and places references directly after limitations following omission of the supplementary sections.

P2.justification: V2 removes the motion-library table, component-ablation table, and RoPE/content-injection/camera-injection visualizations: Tables 8–9 and Figures 12–14. Main Tables 1–7 and Figures 1–11 retain their content and arrangement. Page formatting also changes to larger sheets with substantially wider margins.

improvement.justification: V2 retains the main claims and benchmark scores while removing substantial reproducibility information and controlled evidence supporting important model components. Sections 4.1 and 4.6 still direct readers to the absent supplementary material, leaving metric calculations and additional ablations unavailable in the supplied PDF. Minor editorial fixes do not offset this loss of auditability and empirical support.
